statement: NYG's offence is the worst matchup on the slate against HOU's defence, while NYG's secondary is depleted: expect HOU to win by slightly more than the market has it and NYG to score less.

shift.basis: analyst range, points on the market centre (home = HOU). Sized to a fraction of the adjusted matchup gaps, not taken from them: the market has already moved the HOU side 2-4c and the total down 3-7c since the first capture.

measured.claim: NYG offence vs HOU defence, schedule-adjusted: neutral-script -0.12, pass -0.115, run -0.097 EPA/play (worst pairing on the slate)
NYG out: CB Newsome, S Holland, TE T. Johnson; LB Edmunds IR; CB Adebo, S Nubin and OTs Eluemunor and Mbow questionable. HOU out: RB Montgomery, OT Fisher, S Pitre, S Blankenship
NYG QB has 20 dropbacks this season: no usable pressured/clean split

hypotheses: HOU's pass rush plus NYG's tackle injuries should raise NYG sack and pressure rates beyond the season averages

fail_modes: NYG's defence-and-short-field style keeps the game inside two scores with a backdoor cover
HOU's own losses (Montgomery, Fisher, Dell) lower its ceiling and the favourite gets conservative
garbage-time scoring by the trailing team lifts NYG's total late
challenge.market_already_priced: Partly: the HOU side has moved toward HOU by 2-4c and the total is down 3-7c since the first capture, so the shift range is deliberately smaller than the matchup gaps; the thesis is only the remainder.
challenge.matchup_check: Matchup numbers are the schedule-adjusted ratings (ridge-shrunk, recency-weighted), not raw splits, six games each; NYG QB sample is too small to rely on, so the thesis does not use quarterback efficiency.
uncertainties: fair value is the analyst's shift range through a market-centred simulation, not a validated model

short_reason: NYG's offence is the worst adjusted matchup on the slate (HOU defence) and its secondary is depleted.

statement: Two pass-first offences in a closed dome with DET safety Joseph and GB pass rusher Parsons out: scoring should exceed the market total.

shift.basis: analyst range on the market centre. The total has already risen 3-9c in probability terms since the first capture.

measured.claim: DET offence vs GB defence, adjusted: pass +0.105 EPA/play, neutral-script +0.063
GB offence vs DET defence, adjusted: pass +0.155 EPA/play, neutral-script +0.082
DET S Kerby Joseph out, G Bartch IR; GB pass rusher Parsons, LB Franklin and TE Musgrave out, G Banks questionable

hypotheses: Ford Field's closed roof removes weather as a brake on the passing games

fail_modes: DET's depleted guard depth stalls drives and the game turns into a field-goal game
clock-eating rushing offence from GB with a lead
a defensive or special-teams touchdown swing is noise in either direction
challenge.market_already_priced: Substantially: the total has moved up across the 52-56 rungs since the first capture and now sits above 55, the highest on the slate; the thesis asks whether the market stopped short, which is a thin claim.
challenge.matchup_check: Both pass-offence gaps are schedule-adjusted ratings over 5-6 games; defensive injuries are post-rating information the ratings do not contain.
uncertainties: fair value is the analyst's shift range through a market-centred simulation, not a validated model

short_reason: Two pass-first offences, a closed dome, DET safety Joseph and GB pass rusher Parsons out: scoring above the market total.

statement: SEA's pass rush meets a KC line missing both starting tackles and a quarterback who loses 0.87 EPA/dropback under pressure: SEA should be a little better than the market has it and the game a little lower-scoring.

shift.basis: analyst range on the market centre (home = SEA).

measured.claim: Mahomes: +0.30 EPA/dropback clean, -0.57 under pressure (165 dropbacks); SEA defence QB-hit rate 0.206 and sack rate 0.074, both above the slate means (0.153, 0.063)
KC offence vs SEA defence, schedule-adjusted: pass -0.10, neutral-script -0.11 EPA/play
KC tackles Moore out and Simmons on IR; no OL grade is captured

hypotheses: a depleted KC tackle group leans on chips and quick throws, which blunts the rush

fail_modes: KC's quick-game design neutralises the rush and Mahomes is clean more often than the season rate
the pressured-EPA split is a 165-dropback sample with few pressured snaps
SEA's own QB depth chart shows Lock questionable behind Darnold
challenge.market_already_priced: Unknown: the side has moved 2-5c toward KC and the total down 1-2.5c since the first capture, so the market is not static, but the pressure-versus-tackle matchup is not something a ratings-based price sees.
challenge.matchup_check: The pressure split is a raw (unadjusted) quarterback statistic; the adjusted team pairing is cited beside it. No blitz or coverage data exists, so the thesis does not claim the pressure comes from blitzing.
uncertainties: fair value is the analyst's shift range through a market-centred simulation, not a validated model

short_reason: SEA's pass rush vs a KC line missing both starting tackles; Mahomes is -0.57 EPA/dropback under pressure.

statement: TB's quarterback is questionable and three TB starters are out; the price depends on the inactive list.
blocked_reason: Baker Mayfield (QB, TB) is Questionable. Participation resolves at the inactive list about 90 minutes before the 17:00Z kickoff (about 15:30Z); until then the option value of waiting exceeds any edge, and a player-status-dependent price is not a bet. Re-run at the T-90m horizon.
